Summary (auto): Quick SDK walkthrough focused on getting TidePay engineers up and running with Redwood API and SDKs. Covered Python and TypeScript snippets, environment variables, service accounts, Docker quickstart, and console navigation for routes + Optimize.

00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick off real quick, priya will do the deep dive on the sdk and the code bits
00:18 Mark Chen: Hey thanks, excited to see the quickstart, we want to prototype in the next two weeks, our timeline is pretty tight for the pilot
00:30 Priya Desai: Cool, we'll focus on python and typescript samples, auth patterns, and a small demo of the console. i've got a handout link in the chat -> github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts (note: demo repo is internal shorthand)
00:55 Sara Lopez: the main constraints - sensitive payment PII, we need SOC2 and KMS integration details and region isolation, also low latency for inference under 100ms p95 if possible
01:15 Alex Morgan: noted, we'll cover Dedicated options and private deployment notes later, but first let's get you integrated, one quick q: do you plan to call the hosted api or self-host?
01:30 Mark Chen: prefer hosted for velocity but might move to dedicated if cost/latency doesn't meet SLAs
01:45 Priya Desai: great, so first the python quickstart, i'll paste a short snippet - env var pattern we recommend: REDWOOD_API_KEY or for private deployments REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and REDWOOD_KMS_KEY
02:10 Priya Desai: [code block readout] from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.responses.create(model='redwood-alpha-2', input='Summarize transaction anomalies')
print(resp.output)
02:40 Daniel Reed: quick q — do you support ephemeral tokens / sts so we don't bake long lived keys into containers?
02:50 Priya Desai: yes we do, short-lived tokens via our auth service or integrate with customer's OIDC/SAML for service accounts, we also support integrating with KMS/HSM for encrypting keys at rest
03:10 Alex Morgan: i'll follow up with our security pack, that's the SOC2/ISO docs and a quick guide for KMS wiring
03:30 Priya Desai: typescript example is similar, use @redwood/inference client, snippet:
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.responses.create({ model: 'rwd-2', input: 'Rewrite this email for tone' })
console.log(resp.output)
04:05 Sara Lopez: have you seen issues with node streams and backpressure when streaming responses? our pipeline is heavily stream-based
04:20 Priya Desai: we recommend using the sdk streaming client that emits chunks, there are examples in the repo for node streams + rxjs. for large v2 streams set chunk_size to 512 and handle retry semantics — beware of socket timeouts on older libs
05:00 Mark Chen: how does console route config map to sdk endpoints? we want to auto-route certain requests to cheaper quantized models during low-risk ops
05:15 Alex Morgan: in the console you create routes and attach a model variant; the sdk uses project keys and route ids, so calls can target route-specific policies. Optimize will surface quantization recs by workload and you can pin a route to a cheaper variant with fallback to a larger model
05:45 Priya Desai: i'll show the console in a sec, but for code the route id is passed as route: 'payments-anom-route' in the create call, e.g. client.responses.create({ route: 'payments-anom-route', input: '...' })
06:10 Daniel Reed: ok, that helps. about metrics, we need token-level cost breakdowns for finance and per-route latency histograms for SRE
06:25 Alex Morgan: the console exposes token cost by route and model, plus per-request traces. we can also push traces to your datadog or prometheus via webhooks
06:45 Priya Desai: demo time — switching to my screen to show the repo quickstart, note some of the internal product names may be mis-transcribed in older docs like 'Redwood Dedictaed' you'll see typos but the links are correct
07:10 Priya Desai: showing python quickstart folder: dockerfile, docker-compose, env.example, and tests/benchmark.py which runs sample requests at various concurrency levels
07:40 Priya Desai: env.example uses REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ROUTE_ID, and we suggest storing keys in your cloud secret manager and injecting at deploy time, not baked into image
08:10 Mark Chen: do you have a recommended docker run setup for sidecar auth token refresh?
08:25 Priya Desai: yes we have a small token-refresher sidecar pattern (token-refresh.sh) that requests ephemeral tokens from the auth endpoint and writes to /run/secrets/redwood_token, you mount that as a file and the sdk can read either env var or file path
09:00 Sara Lopez: can you demo the ts quickstart folder?
09:10 Priya Desai: switching, here's ts example with dockerfile and an express sample that streams responses to client web-sockets. we use the official @redwood/inference package published to npm, version pinned in package.json. the quickstart includes a script 'npm run local' which sets NODE_ENV=development and reads .env.local
09:40 Alex Morgan: a note about versioning — we recommend pinning the sdk version and the model version in package.json and deployment manifests, then use semantic versioning for rollouts. the console supports canary routing too
10:05 Mark Chen: for the pilot, we expect to send about 150 RPS at peak, average payload 200 tokens, can you help estimate cost?
10:25 Alex Morgan: we'll model that in the pricing sheet; rough calc: at hosted rates that maps to ~X tokens/day, priya will run a quickbench script to estimate tokens/sec and latency for rwd-2 quantized vs full fp16
10:50 Priya Desai: let's run a quick local benchmark using the included benchmark.py, it simulates concurrency with async workers and prints p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec. if you want we'll run in our infra later for exact numbers
11:40 Daniel Reed: about network egress and data residency, do you offer regional endpoints? we need EU-only data flows for some markets
11:52 Alex Morgan: yes, regional endpoints and VPC/private deployment is available; for EU-only we can set up a private control plane with data processing in eu-west, and Dedicated pools in customer-specified regions. will include in the follow-up doc
12:20 Sara Lopez: on security — how do audit logs surface? we need decryptable traces for forensics but not raw PII in logs
12:35 Alex Morgan: audit logs are available in the console and can be exported to S3 with encryption via your KMS key, redact sensitive fields at the route-level, and long-term retention is configurable. we'll include recommended retentions in the SOC2 pack
13:05 Priya Desai: quick demo of the console: routes tab, model catalog, Optimize suggestions - you can click a workload and it shows batch/quantization recs and estimated cost savings. note: Optimize suggestions are heuristics based on seq length and token distribution, you should validate quality with your eval prompts
14:00 Mark Chen: what about function calling or tool-calls? we need structured responses for our downstream reconciliation systems
14:15 Priya Desai: our responses API supports structured outputs and function/tool calling; the TS client has a helper to map schema to typed responses. also suggest adding unit tests in the quickstart to validate structure using our eval harness
15:00 Alex Morgan: let's talk auth patterns for CI/CD and workers: recommended is service account keys for servers (rotated monthly) and ephemeral tokens for front-end user requests, plus OIDC for internal auth flows
15:25 Daniel Reed: is there a recommended token rotation cadence with the sidecar?
15:35 Priya Desai: sidecar refresh every 15 minutes by default, but you can set to shorter if you have stricter limits. TTLs are configurable on the auth service
16:00 Sara Lopez: any gotchas migrating from older SDK versions or open-source clients?
16:15 Priya Desai: watch for breaking changes in streaming APIs (older clients had different chunk events), also some older doc references to 'kv cache' may be abbreviated and confusing, our migration guide covers it
16:50 Priya Desai: live code snippet — running docker-compose up (shows logs) and then curl to local endpoint, response stream arrives in chunks, printed as they come
18:10 Mark Chen: latency looked good locally, but we want end-to-end under 100ms p95 including network; are dedicated pools single-tenant for latency predictability?
18:25 Alex Morgan: Dedicated pools are isolated GPU pools with predictable throughput and can give lower p95; also enable autoscaling and burst capacity for traffic spikes. we'll include SKU options for dedicated in the price appendix
19:00 Daniel Reed: cost vs latency question — if we quantize aggressively we save costs but risk hallucination. how do you balance that?
19:20 Priya Desai: Optimize gives quantization recommendations but we pair that with evals; you should run a small eval set (we have an eval harness in the repo) and look for regressions. fallback policies are recommended: route to quantized model normally, and fallback to full model when confidence low or certain inputs match high-risk patterns
20:05 Alex Morgan: i'll send the pricing sheet with scenarios: hosted + dedicated delta + expected savings with optimize, and include an SOW option for pilot benchmarking
20:30 Priya Desai: quickly covering diagnostics: per-request traces include model_id, route_id, token counts, and latency, and you can tag requests with metadata. we also support sampling for full-text logs to protect PII
21:10 Mark Chen: ok good. regarding onboarding, what's the typical timeline to go from PoC to pilot?
21:25 Alex Morgan: typically 2-6 weeks for a pilot depending on benchmarks and legal review, security checks can add 1-2 weeks for enterprise customers, Private deployments take longer due to network setup
21:50 Priya Desai: demo end — i'll paste links to the quickstart repo, console docs, and a checklist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts, https://docs.redwood.ai/console, https://docs.redwood.ai/security/soc2-checklist
22:10 Sara Lopez: can you share the api contract for streaming responses? i'd like to add it to our integration spec
22:25 Priya Desai: yes i'll add a code snippet and a link to the streaming api section in the quickstart README

23:20 Mark Chen: loop in me and daniel, and our security lead amy will be cc'd after i share her contact
23:40 Alex Morgan: perfect, we'll target the benchmark week of 6/15, and priya will run initial bench and share results 6/10

24:10 Daniel Reed: just one more, offline — do you have a terraform module for the secret injection and route creation?
24:20 Priya Desai: yes we have terraform modules and cloudformation snippets, i'll include them in the repo under infra/terraform
